action.default: absent -> "command 'camera' : action argument"; present with any other word -> "command 'camera' : missing name" when no `name` was given, else "command 'camera' : unknown action argument"
action.doc: What to do with the point of view; every other key on the line depends on this word.
action.source: app_command_interface.cpp:4233, 4236-4239, 4241, 4252, 4276, 4311, 4375, 4390, 4405, 4415, 4443, 4466-4506 (W_ROTATE="rotate", W_ALIGN_WITH="align_with", W_TRANSITION_TO="transition_to", W_MOVE_TO="move_to", W_SAVE="save", W_LOAD="load", W_FREE_MODE="free_mode", W_DESCEND="descend", W_LIFT_OFF="lift_off", W_CREATE="create", W_DROP="drop", W_SWITCH="switch", W_FOLLOW_ROTATION="follow_rotation": base_command_interface.hpp:151,248,247,246,144,103,242,243,245,222,152,225,241)

value_docs.align_with: tilt the view so that the named place's own up direction becomes yours, over `duration` seconds
value_docs.create: declare a new named place the view can be attached to
value_docs.descend: go down towards, or up away from, what you are looking at
value_docs.follow_rotation: say whether the view turns with the body it is attached to
value_docs.free_mode: switch free flight on or off
value_docs.lift_off: climb to a given height and then detach the view from the body
value_docs.load: put the view back where such a file says
value_docs.move_to: travel to a point of space or to a body, over `duration`
value_docs.rotate: turn the view towards the place you are standing on, over `duration` seconds
value_docs.save: write where the view is, and when, into a file
value_docs.switch: attach the view to a named place
value_docs.transition_to: change what the view is attached to, without travelling: either the place you stand right now, or a body

altitude.default: on `move_to target body`: absent -> stop at five times the body's own radius; on `lift_off`: absent -> "command 'camera lift_off' : missing altitude"
altitude.doc: On `move_to`, how high above the body to stop, in kilometres; on `lift_off`, the height to climb to, in whatever unit the `moveto` command reads (see notes).
altitude.notes: On `lift_off` the value is not used directly: it is written into a `moveto altitude <value> duration <duration>` line (:4459), i.e. it becomes the `moveto` command's own altitude argument (unit 3).
altitude.source: app_command_interface.cpp:4354, 4358-4361 (move_to body), 4390, 4393-4396, 4404 (lift_off) -> src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:475 ('alt/AU', with AU in kilometres, src/tools/sc_const.hpp:45) (W_ALTITUDE="altitude", base_command_interface.hpp:175)
altitude.value_domain: number(evalDouble) -- $-variable substitution possible; kilometres on `move_to target body` [derived: the value is divided by AU, and AU is declared in kilometres]

body.doc: On `action align_with`, the name of the place (declared with `action create`, of the kind that follows a body) whose up direction the view should take.
body.notes: Despite the key name it is looked up among the declared PLACES, not among the bodies, and the place must be one that follows a body; otherwise the log says "anchor not found" / "wrong anchor type" and the command reports "error align_with_body body".

body_name.default: absent -> "command 'move_to body' : missing a body_name or time"
body_name.doc: On `action move_to target body`, which body to travel to.
body_name.notes: As with `body` above, the name is looked up among the declared PLACES that follow a body (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:491-497), so only bodies that have such a place declared can be travelled to.

coef.doc: On `action descend`, how much closer to go: less than 1 goes down, more than 1 goes up (0.5 halves the distance, 2 doubles it).
coef.notes: What it goes down towards depends on where you are: the ground under the view ray when a body is close, the last selected body when you are out among the systems (src/experimentalModule/Camera.cpp:728-742). New drawing path only.

coord_func.default: absent -> no orbit can be built and the place is not created
coord_func.doc: On `action create` with type orbit, which kind of orbit describes the movement.
coord_func.notes: The orbit's own numbers are the same keys a body's orbit uses (INTENT S5 item 4) -- see `flagged`.
coord_func.value_domain: string -- the orbit-kind names of the stellar-system-file grammar

duration.default: on `rotate`: absent -> 2 seconds; on `align_with`: absent -> 0 (immediate); on `move_to target point`: absent -> the jump is immediate; on `move_to target body`: absent -> "command 'move_to body' : missing a body_name or time"; on `lift_off`: absent -> 3 seconds
duration.doc: How long the movement takes, in seconds.
duration.notes: On both `move_to` forms the script ALSO waits: the delay before the next command is set to this many seconds (:4337, :4366 -- evalInt(value) x 1000 milliseconds, so a fractional duration is cut down to whole seconds for the wait but not for the movement). The travel itself is measured in simulated time: the seconds are divided by 86400 and the arrival is that many days later on the simulation clock (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:430, 464).

filename.default: on `action save`: absent -> the name 'anchor' (src/coreModule/coreLink.hpp:371); on `action load`: absent -> "command 'camera load' : missing file name"
filename.doc: The file to write the view into, or to read it back from.
filename.notes: The file written holds the place's declaration plus your height, longitude, latitude, the date and the direction you look in (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:722-733). DEFECT, recorded not fixed: the folder 'anchors/' is prepended TWICE on both paths (src/coreModule/coreLink.cpp:65 and src/bodyModule/ssystem_factory.hpp:740; likewise :72 and :744), so the file actually used is anchors/anchors/<name>, relative to the folder the program was started in.

follow_rotation.default: absent -> the place does not declare it
follow_rotation.doc: On `action create` with type body, whether the place turns with the body.

name.default: absent -> the four forms that need it are refused with "command 'camera' : missing name", which is ALSO what an unknown action reports
name.doc: The name of a place the view can be attached to (its own name, not a body's).
name.notes: On `action transition_to target body` the same key means a BODY name instead (:4293) -- the only place in this handler where it does.

orbit_center_x.default: absent -> the place is not created
orbit_center_x.doc: On `action create` with type orbit and no parent, the centre of the orbit: first coordinate, in astronomical units.

orbit_center_y.default: absent -> the place is not created
orbit_center_y.doc: On `action create` with type orbit and no parent, the centre of the orbit: second coordinate, in astronomical units.

orbit_center_z.default: absent -> the place is not created
orbit_center_z.doc: On `action create` with type orbit and no parent, the centre of the orbit: third coordinate, in astronomical units.

parent.default: absent -> the orbit must instead be given a centre with orbit_center_x/y/z
parent.doc: On `action create` with type orbit, the body the orbit goes around.

state.doc: On `action free_mode`, whether free flight is on.
state.notes: Same silent-off class as `flag`: a typo means 'off' with no diagnostic. New drawing path only.
values: on-forms per Utility::isTrue = free flight on

target.default: absent -> "command 'camera' : missing target" (rotate: "missing target"; transition_to and move_to: their own message); present with any other word -> "command 'transition_to' : unknown target arg" / "command 'camera' : unknown target arg"
target.notes: ON `action rotate` THE VALUE IS NOT USED: it must be non-empty, but the movement always goes to the place you are standing on -- Core::lookAnchor ignores its name argument (the per-name branch is commented out, src/coreModule/core.cpp:2709-2719).

value_docs.body: a body: named by `name` on `transition_to`, by `body_name` on `move_to`
value_docs.point: on `transition_to`: the exact place you are standing right now becomes a named place called temp_point; on `move_to`: the point given by `x`, `y` and `z`

type.default: absent -> the place is not created; both registries log what was expected
type.doc: On `action create`, what kind of place is being declared.

value_docs.body: a place attached to the body named by body_name
value_docs.observatory: a fixed place, given by x, y and z (the same thing as point for the newer drawing path)
value_docs.orbit: a place that follows an orbit, around parent or around the fixed point orbit_center_x/y/z
value_docs.point: a fixed place, given by x, y and z

value.doc: On `action follow_rotation`, whether the view turns with the body: write exactly the word true for yes.
value.notes: SHARP EDGE: this is the only boolean of the unit that is NOT read with the usual on/1/true grammar -- the test is an exact string comparison against `true`, so `on`, `1` and `TRUE` all mean NO here.

x.doc: On `action move_to target point`, where to go: the first coordinate, counted from the Sun.
x.notes: The three numbers are a position in the heliocentric ecliptic frame (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:387-395, 405-442). The unit is NOT stated on this path: astronomical units is [derived] from two facts about the same frame -- the km->AU divisor applied to `altitude` beside it (src/navModule/anchor_manager.cpp:475, with AU declared in kilometres at src/tools/sc_const.hpp:45), and the new-path anchor code, which says 'a fixed point x/y/z in AU' of the same coordinates (src/experimentalModule/CameraAnchors.cpp:100). On `action create` the same three spellings are read again downstream, for a fixed place (see the downstream keys).

y.doc: On `action move_to target point`, where to go: the second coordinate, counted from the Sun.

z.doc: On `action move_to target point`, where to go: the third coordinate, counted from the Sun.

doc: Move the point of view about the universe: name a place, go to it, turn towards a body, or fly up from where you stand.
name: camera
